newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil battles in court to win CVRD privatization.
newsitem.headline: Brazil battles in court to win CVRD privatization.

text.p: Brazil will insist on Wednesday in its efforts to try and auction mining conglomerate Companhia do Vale do Rio Doce one day after those opposed to the sale succeeded in stopping it in the courts.
Brazil's National Development Bank (BNDES), which is responsible for managing CVRD sale, has rescheduled the privatization auction for 1000 local/1300 GMT at the Rio de Janeiro Stock Exchange.
But first the government must convince the Superior Court of Justice (STJ) to overrule up to four injunctions blocking the sale which have been logged in lower courts.

On Tuesday the government failed to convince the STJ to throw out an injunction issued by a Sao Paulo Federal Court which ruled the CVRD sale could be a threat to national interests and has been the main obstacle preventing the auction from taking place.

In a television interview this morning Planning Minister Antonio Kandir denied the government had been caught flat footed before a flurry of court actions designed to stop the CVRD sale, which had originally been scheduled to take place on Tuesday.
"This was not a defeat. We expected this to happen," Kandir said.
"What is important is that the auction take place, and the sooner the better."
According to news reports on Tuesday the STJ threw out 11 court rulings which were opposed to the CVRD selloff.

This morning Rio de Janeiro city authorities re-enforced security in the area surrounding the stock exchange after several people were hurt on Tuesday in clashes between police and demonstrators opposed to the CVRD sale.
While virtually all the 53 companies sold-off under Brazil's six year-old privatization program have met some kind of resistance, none have generated the opposition of the CVRD sale.

With over 15,400 employees and an annual turnover of more than $5.0 billion, CVRD was unusual among most Brazilian state companies in that it was profitable and generally considered an example of good management.
Besides aluminium, paper and pulp holdings, the company's Carajas mine contains the world's biggest iron ore deposits as well as considerable gold, bauxite, manganese reserves.
Paradoxically, some analysts saw a silver lining in the postponement of Tuesday's auction.
They said the delays would allow one of the two groups which have registered to bid in the CVRD auction more time to reorganize their consortium.

According to news reports, Companhia Suzano de Papel e Celulose, one of the key partners in the the consortia led by Brazilian steel mill Companhia Siderurgica Nacional (CSN) , on Tuesday announced it was dropping out of the contest.
Suzano was the second defection from the CSN-led consortium after U.S. aluminium concern Alcoa decided to drop out last week.
Analysts are widely predicting the auction will be won by the Valecom consortium, which is led by Brazil's Grupo Votorantim paper, pulp and cement holding.
